correctness.rationale: Normalized concentric annulus has covariance (1+r²)I/4, so affine projection kernel K_r(x,y)=1+x·y/b, b=(1+r²)/4. Along a fixed direction the Lebesgue integral of |1+c·y| is even convex in evaluation radius, so its essential supremum is at the outer circle. Kernel symmetry/duality equates endpoint norms. Negative kernel cap gives Λ=1+2[H(1,b)−H(r,b)]/[πb(1−r²)], H(R,b)=2∫_b^R(z−b)√(R²−z²)dz; the claimed antiderivative is exact. In s=r² and uniform radial area parameter u, Λ=1+(2/π)∫G(c_s(u))du; ∂_s c_s has exactly one sign change and G′ is increasing, yielding strict negative weighted integral since ∫c_s strictly decreases. Tangency r=b occurs at 2−√3; elementary cap substitution yields a positive (r−r*)_+^(5/2) coefficient, analytic remainder and precisely C²/non-C³ cusp. Boundary r=1 is a limiting measure, not area normalization. Independent quadrature/series checks support but do not prove universal assertions.
residual_risks: Numerical monotonicity grids do not prove strictness; proof relies on analytic one-sign-change inequality.
